requirement.evidence: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
requirement.note: Cap, CPI adjustment starting January 1 of year after enactment (2027 follows from approval Jan 20, 2026), and refund from penalty are supported. But the document says the Director/Attorney General bring complaints and a mechanism for applicants to report violations is set by rules; whether applicants can report to the Division is only via rulemaking, not yet stated as in effect.

key_value.evidence: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
key_value.note: The $50 cap is stated; the annual CPI adjustment is stated in subsection d.

effective_date.evidence: 3.  This act shall take effect on the first day of the fourth month next following the date of enactment, except that the Director of the Division of Consumer Affairs in the Department of Law and Public Safety shall be permitted to take anticipatory action necessary to effectuate the provisions of this act.
effective_date.note: With approval on January 20, 2026, the first day of the fourth month next following is May 1, 2026. This is computed, and the enactment date is the approval date by small inference.

coverage.evidence:
(1) a dwelling unit
located in a one-family or two-family dwelling that is offered for rent; or
coverage.note: The document exempts one- and two-family dwellings, so coverage would be buildings of 3+ units, but it also exempts New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees who are not the landlord. The card's min_units 3 is only a rough inference and omits the licensee exemption; no unit threshold is stated as such.
